# Streaming answers

A model writes its answer a few words at a time. `$llm.text.streamAsync()` hands you each piece as it's written, so a page
can show the answer as it appears instead of after a wait:

```ts
const r: LlmTextAnswer = await $llm.text.streamAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: question }, (text) => {
  // called with each piece, in order; return false to stop the answer there
})
// r is the whole answer, as $llm.text.completeAsync returns it
```

```go
s, err := textv1.Contract.Must(app).Stream(ctx, extkit.Internal, textv1.CompleteInput{Model: "vultr/glm-5.3", Prompt: question})
if err != nil {
	return err
}
var r *textv1.CompleteResult
err = s.Run(ctx, func(e any) error {
	c := e.(textv1.Chunk) // a piece of text, in order; the last one is Done, with the whole answer
	if c.Done {
		r = c.Result
	}
	return nil // an error stops the answer there
})
```

A third argument, `onReasoning`, gets the model's thinking as it's written, when the provider sends it. The callbacks
run on the app's JS VM between pieces; the waiting for each piece doesn't, so other requests are served meanwhile.

## In a page

A Pages API route forwards the pieces to the browser as server-sent events:

```ts
// pb_pages/ask.ts
module.exports = {
  async post(ctx) {
    const { question } = ctx.req.body()
    const stream = ctx.res.sse()
    try {
      const r: LlmTextAnswer = await $llm.text.streamAsync({ model: "vultr/glm-5.3", prompt: question }, (text) => stream.send("text", JSON.stringify(text)))
      stream.send("done", JSON.stringify({ usage: r.usage }))
    } catch (err: any) {
      stream.send("error", JSON.stringify(String(err.message || err)))
    }
    stream.close()
  },
}
```

In the browser, read the response as it arrives:

```js
// in the browser
const res = await fetch("/ask", { method: "POST", headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body: JSON.stringify({ question }) })
const reader = res.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader()
let buf = "", answer = ""
for (;;) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read()
  if (done) break
  buf += value
  let i
  while ((i = buf.indexOf("\n\n")) >= 0) {
    const block = buf.slice(0, i)
    buf = buf.slice(i + 2)
    const event = (block.match(/^event: (.*)$/m) || [])[1]
    const data = (block.match(/^data: (.*)$/m) || [])[1]
    if (event === "text") answer += JSON.parse(data) // show it
  }
}
```

The browser's `EventSource` only makes GET requests, which is why this reads the stream with `fetch`.

## Over HTTP

Outside your app's code, `POST /api/_c/llm.text/v1/stream` does the same, with the same body as `complete`, as a
superuser or with a token that has the `llm` scope. Each piece is an `event: stream` with `{"text": "..."}`, and the
last one is `{"done": true, "result": {...}}`.
